statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-70162 (GHSA-2fmv-rv2c-59x7) is a .NET denial of service issue in System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs: on Windows, EnvelopedCms.Decode can do quadratic work on attacker-supplied CMS or PKCS#7 attributes. Microsoft lists Windows as the only affected platform, and the CVE record lists the package on .NET runtimes installed on Windows (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2fmv-rv2c-59x7, https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-70162, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/454). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux. Scanned all 264 packages of the published builds (10.0.2-r0, 10.0.3-r0, 10.0.4-r0, 10.0.5-r0, 10.0.6-r0, 10.0.7-r0, 10.0.8-r0, 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold. Implementation copies of System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs.dll come in two builds. The portable build is the one a .NET runtime on Linux loads: it is in the Microsoft.AspNetCore.App shared framework (aspnetcore10-runtime, and the .NET SDK and the ASP.NET Core runtime archive held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap), the ASP.NET Core runtime pack and the SDK's own and F# directories in dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap, and in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts the lib/ folders of the System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs nupkg and the ASP.NET Core transport nupkg and the tools/ folders of build-tool nupkg files. It makes no calls into the Windows crypt32 library (checked in the shared framework of the 10.0.2-r0 x86_64 and 10.0.15-r0 aarch64 aspnetcore10-runtime packages and in every portable copy in the 10.0.13-r0 x86_64 dotnet10-runtime-artifacts package). The Windows build, which does call crypt32, is present only as runtimes/win assets in the SDK and in nupkg files, which .NET selects only when running on Windows, and in the lib/ folder of the WindowsDesktop transport nupkg used to build the Windows desktop framework. The remaining copies are reference assemblies with no implementation code. So the Windows-only code path is not reached on these Linux builds.
